source_method: Modern Flora of North America, Flora of China and botanical institutional treatments; genus-level, historical and variety-level evidence distinguished and uncertainty held.

sources.reference: Flora of North America, Helenium genus key
sources.scope: key-to-species character contrast; not full species account

morphology.stems: Winged from decurrent leaf bases (genus key branch)
morphology.leaves: Distal blades entire, contrasted with serrate distal blades of H. microcephalum
morphology.heads: Heads radiate, 10–15 yellow-to-variegated rays in FNA key
morphology.disk: Disk-floret corolla lobes four, versus often five in H. microcephalum
morphology.fruit: Pappus non-aristate scales by keyed lineage; specific dimensions unconfirmed

holds: Modern species-specific height, involucral measurements and geography not confirmed; preserve field descriptions as provisional.
Existing learner description calls disk elongated; not newly verified by genus key.

sources.reference: Flora of North America, Heterotheca genus key and sect. Phyllotheca
sources.scope: genus key characters specific to H. villosa

sources.reference: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center, Heterotheca villosa

morphology.height: FNA key (5–)16–40(–70) cm, not invariant across varieties
morphology.stems: Ascending or spreading leafy branches, short-strigose/hispid
morphology.leaves: Mid/distal alternate leaves usually lanceolate to oblanceolate/oblong, sparsely to densely hispido-strigose, may be glandular
morphology.heads: Yellow radiate heads, 1–20(–70) per plant in FNA key; disk also yellow
morphology.rays: Ray ligules (3.5–)5–11(–20) mm across keyed close species group
morphology.fruit: Ray and disc cypselae with pappus bristles (sect. Phyllotheca); inner pappus bristles at least as long as corollas

holds: FNA explicitly describes large infraspecific variation; keyed measurements not guaranteed for each variety.

sources.reference: Flora of North America, Solidago juliae treatment
sources.scope: species account; accessible indexed opening and repository prior FNA-derived characteristics

morphology.height: 50–250 cm in existing documented FNA-derived source record
morphology.stem: Uniform dense soft white villoso-tomentose hairs with crisped/thin hairs, distinctive against glabrate S. gigantea
morphology.leaves: Alternate narrow lanceolate 3-veined leaves 50–80(–120) × 5–10(–12) mm, with sparse/moderate dentition and bilateral hairs
morphology.inflorescence: Narrow pyramidal panicle about 3–4× as long as wide, 80–950 heads, involucres about 3–4 mm
morphology.habitat: Edwards Plateau/Trans-Pecos streams/lakes, grassland and woodland; not solely xeric

holds: Numeric traits are supported by preexisting repository FNA-provenanced morphology and indexed FNA source; full FNA page fetch failed in this pass.
Do not mistake damp stream sites for excluding S. juliae.

sources.reference: Flora of China, Sphagneticola trilobata species treatment
Flora of North America, Sphagneticola trilobata
Royal Botanic Gardens Kew POWO Sphagneticola trilobata

morphology.habit: Creeping mat-forming perennial, stems rooting at nodes, with ascending flowering shoots
morphology.leaves: Opposite, somewhat thick/succulent, sessile or petiole <5 mm; elliptic/lanceolate, frequently 3-lobed and toothed, up to 18 cm in flora treatment
morphology.heads: Solitary heads on long stalks, involucral phyllaries lanceolate approximately 10–15 mm
morphology.rays: Four to eight conspicuous fertile yellow rays, ligules 15–20 mm with 3–4 teeth
morphology.disk: Numerous bisexual yellow disk florets; tubular corollas 5–6 mm
morphology.fruit: Dark angled club-shaped cypsela about 5 mm, pappus fused scale-like crown

holds: Native in tropical Americas but widely introduced elsewhere; do not infer native status in Hays County.
Source reports 'disk florets ca. 2 cm' ambiguously; avoid this likely head-size confusion and keep only confirmed corolla 5–6 mm.

sources.reference: Flora of North America Tetraneuris acaulis species treatment replicated in World Flora Online
Flora of North America Tetraneuris acaulis variety key

morphology.habit: Perennial 2–30+ cm from usually branched thickening caudices
morphology.leaves: All basal in rosette, spatulate/oblanceolate to narrow linear-oblanceolate, entire, variably hairy and gland-dotted
morphology.stems: 1–35(–60) mostly unbranched head-bearing scapes, peduncles 0.5–30 cm
morphology.heads: Single yellow radiate head per scape, involucre 7–12 × 8–16 mm
morphology.disk: 25–200+ disk florets, yellow tubular corollas 2.7–4.3 mm
morphology.fruit: Cypselae 2–4 mm, pappus of five to eight aristate scales 2.2–3.7 mm

holds: Four varieties recognized by FNA; do not identify var. acaulis from the broad species description.
County-level BONAP nativity deferred, existing learner cautions Panhandle emphasis.

sources.reference: Flora of North America Trixis californica var. californica
Flora of North America, Trixis genus and species key

morphology.habit: Shrub, 20–200 cm for FNA var. californica, glandular and pubescent
morphology.leaves: Cauline, ascending nearly parallel to stems; winged petiole 1.5–5 mm and narrow lanceolate blades 2–11 cm, entire to faintly toothed/revolute in var. californica
morphology.heads: Quasi-radiate, in corymbiform/paniculiform arrays, phyllaries usually 8 and 8–14 mm long for var. californica
morphology.florets: Eleven to 25 florets in var. californica, yellow bilateral 2-lipped corollas with outer 3-lobed lip; unlike ordinary ray/disk Asteraceae pattern
morphology.fruits: Cypselae 6–10.5 mm with mucilage-forming papilla-like hairs when wet, pappus 7.5–12 mm in var. californica
morphology.habitat: Dry rocky slopes, washes and thorn scrub in southwestern US/Mexico

holds: Most numeric metrics are variety californica only; species-level learner must retain varietal scope.
